title: Engineering Spec Schema — BRD to Build/QA/Deploy/Cutover/Hypercare
description: Schema for a machine-executable engineering spec for a web SaaS application. Claude Code reads this schema, ingests a BRD plus supporting documents, and produces a spec document that validates against it. The same spec document is then consumed by Claude Code sessions to build, test, deploy, cut over, and run hypercare. Every field carries x-instructions (how to populate it), x-source (where the content comes from), and x-phase (which delivery phase consumes it).

x-claude-code-protocol.purpose: Ordered procedure for the spec-generation session.
steps: 1. INGEST: Read the BRD and every supporting doc listed by the user. Build an inventory of every stated business requirement; assign each a stable id (BRD-001, BRD-002, ...) in the traceability_matrix, quoting the source sentence and doc/section.

2. DECOMPOSE: Convert requirements into spec_items. One item = one independently buildable and testable unit (a feature slice, an API, a data model, an integration, an NFR, an ops task). Split anything that cannot be verified by a single set of acceptance criteria.

3. FILL: Populate every field of every spec_item per that field's x-instructions. Facts come only from the inputs (x-source: brd/docs). Engineering judgment fields (x-source: derived) must be justified in-line. Never invent business facts — if the BRD is silent, write 'TBD' and register an entry in open_questions with a proposed default.

4. TRACE: Every spec_item must list at least one brd_requirement_id, or set item_type to a technical/ops type and state in summary why it exists (e.g. 'enabling infrastructure'). Every BRD requirement must be covered by at least one spec_item or explicitly listed in product_overview.out_of_scope.
5. VALIDATE: Check the finished document against this schema, then against the x-quality-gates below. Fix all violations before emitting.
6. EMIT: Write spec.json (this document) and a human-readable spec.md rendered from it. spec.json is the source of truth; spec.md is a view.
x-claude-code-protocol.execution_contract: Downstream build/QA/deploy sessions treat spec.json as authoritative. They pick spec_items in dependency order, flip status as work progresses, and must not change requirement content without recording a change_log entry and bumping the item's version.

x-quality-gates: No required field contains 'TBD' when spec_meta.status is 'approved'.
Every acceptance_criteria entry is Given/When/Then and objectively verifiable by an automated test or a scripted manual check.
Every data entity field has a type and nullability; every API endpoint has request/response shapes and error codes.
Every spec_item with db_changes has migration_steps and a rollback_plan.
Every user-facing spec_item has accessibility and responsive_behavior filled (not 'N/A').
traceability_matrix covers 100% of BRD requirement ids with no orphans in either direction.
cutover_plan and hypercare_plan are present and non-empty before spec_meta.status may be 'approved'.

spec_meta.description: Identity and lifecycle of the spec document itself.

spec_version.description: Semver. Bump minor on item additions, major on scope changes.

approvers.description: Humans who must sign off before status = approved.

inputs.description: The documents this spec was derived from. Everything in the spec must trace back here or be marked derived.

supporting_docs.description: Wireframes, brand guides, compliance docs, existing-system docs, API docs of third parties, etc.

product_overview.description: One-page framing distilled from the BRD.

success_metrics.x-instructions: Business KPIs from the BRD, each with a measurable target and measurement method. These feed hypercare_plan.success_review.

out_of_scope.x-instructions: Include every BRD requirement deliberately excluded, with the reason.

constraints.description: Budget, timeline, mandated tech, regulatory constraints from the BRD.

architecture.description: System-level decisions that individual spec_items inherit. Decide once here, reference from items.

stack.x-instructions: Honor any stack mandated by the BRD/constraints; otherwise choose and justify in decision_records.

authn_authz_model.description: How users sign in, session model, role/permission model, tenant isolation of authz.

multi_tenancy_model.description: SaaS tenancy: shared-schema with tenant_id, schema-per-tenant, etc., and the isolation guarantees.

integration_map.description: All third-party services and the direction of data flow.

decision_records.x-instructions: Record every non-obvious derived choice so humans can veto at review.

environments.description: Environment matrix used by build, QA and deploy phases.

data_policy.description: Real vs synthetic data; PII handling per environment.

deploy_trigger.description: e.g. push to main, manual promote, PR preview.

spec_items.description: The core of the spec: the work-item table. Each item carries the full column set below (the '60-odd columns').

traceability_matrix.description: BRD requirement inventory with forward links into spec_items.

requirement_text.description: Verbatim or tightly paraphrased from the BRD.

covered_by.description: spec_ids, or the literal string 'OUT-OF-SCOPE' with the exclusion listed in product_overview.out_of_scope.

release_plan.description: How spec_items group into releases and the order of build.

milestones.x-instructions: Order by dependency graph, then priority. Milestone 1 should be a walking skeleton: auth + tenancy + one end-to-end slice deployed to staging.

definition_of_done.description: Global DoD applied to every spec_item in addition to its own acceptance criteria (tests pass, lint clean, deployed to staging, docs updated...).

cutover_plan.description: Go-live procedure. Consumed by the deploy/cutover phase.

strategy.description: Big-bang, phased, parallel-run, or dark launch — and why.

prerequisites.description: DNS, TLS, prod env vars, third-party prod credentials, legal/compliance sign-offs, billing live-mode keys.

data_migration.x-instructions: If greenfield with no legacy data, state that explicitly rather than omitting.

runbook.x-instructions: Numbered, executable steps. Mark any step Claude cannot perform (DNS registrar, payment provider dashboard) as owner: human.

rollback.description: Trigger conditions and exact procedure to return to pre-cutover state, including data implications.

comms.description: Who is told what, when: users, stakeholders, status page.

hypercare_plan.description: Elevated-support period after go-live. Consumed by the hypercare phase.

monitoring.x-instructions: Cover at minimum: error rate, p95 latency, uptime, signup/login success, payment success (if billing), queue/job backlogs.

hotfix_procedure.description: Fast path to production for hypercare fixes, including reduced-but-not-zero QA bar.

known_issues_log.description: Where deferred defects are tracked during hypercare.

success_review.description: How product_overview.success_metrics get measured at hypercare end.

exit_criteria.description: Conditions to leave hypercare and enter normal operations.

open_questions.description: Everything the inputs did not answer. Blockers for approval, not for drafting.

question_id.description: Stable id referenced by spec_items.open_question_refs. Never reused.

context.description: Why it matters; which spec_ids depend on it.

proposed_default.x-instructions: Always propose a sensible default so the human can approve with one word.

blocking.description: true if build cannot start on affected items without an answer.

glossary.description: Domain and product terms used consistently across all spec_items.

doc_id.description: Short handle used in source_references, e.g. 'BRD', 'WIREFRAMES'.

authority.description: binding docs win conflicts; informative docs are context only.

specItem.description: One unit of buildable, testable work. The property set below is the spec's column definition (~64 columns across 8 groups).

spec_id.description: Stable unique id. Never reused, never renumbered.

summary.description: 2-3 sentences: what and why. Readable without opening the BRD.

detailed_description.description: Full behavioral description in plain prose. The builder should need no other narrative.

epic.description: Parent grouping for roll-up reporting; matches release_plan milestones where possible.

brd_requirement_ids.description: Traceability links (BRD-xxx). Empty only for purely technical/ops items — say why in summary.

source_references.description: doc_id + section for every non-BRD input used, e.g. 'WIREFRAMES p.4'.

assumptions.x-instructions: Every gap you filled with judgment gets a line here. Assumptions are veto-able at review.

out_of_scope.description: Adjacent behavior explicitly NOT included in this item, to stop scope creep in build.

open_question_refs.description: question_ids from the top-level open_questions (Q-xxx) that affect this item.

priority.x-instructions: MoSCoW. Derive from BRD language; when ambiguous choose lower priority and log an open question.

priority_rationale.description: One line: business value driving the priority.

complexity_estimate.description: Relative build effort. XL items should usually be split.

dependencies.description: spec_ids that must be built first, plus external dependencies prefixed 'ext:' (e.g. 'ext: Stripe account created — human provisions').

status.x-instructions: Lifecycle flag flipped by downstream sessions. Spec generation always emits 'draft'.

version.description: Item-level version; bump on any requirement change after approval and add a change_log entry.

owner.description: Who executes. human_gate = Claude builds, human must approve before production.

user_stories.description: 'As a <persona>, I want <goal>, so that <benefit>.' Personas must exist in product_overview.target_users.

actors.description: Roles/systems that interact with this behavior, including scheduled jobs and webhooks.

preconditions.description: State that must hold before the flow starts (auth state, plan tier, feature flag, data present).

main_flow.description: Numbered happy-path steps from trigger to postcondition.

alternate_flows.description: Branches: cancel, retry, empty state, concurrent edit, permission variant.

business_rules.description: Deterministic rules: validation limits, calculations, entitlements, quotas. Exact numbers, no adjectives.

edge_cases.x-instructions: Enumerate aggressively: empty, max-length, unicode, timezone, duplicate submit, expired session, deleted tenant, race conditions.

error_handling.description: For each failure mode: what the user sees (exact copy tone), what is logged, whether it retries, terminal state.

acceptance_criteria.x-instructions: Given/When/Then, objectively verifiable. These become the QA phase's test oracle — write them so a test can be generated mechanically.

ui_screens.description: Screens/routes touched, with wireframe refs from source_references where available.

ui_components.description: Reusable components introduced or modified; note design-system source.

ui_states.description: Loading, empty, error, success, and permission-denied states for each screen.

accessibility.x-instructions: WCAG 2.1 AA baseline unless BRD says otherwise: keyboard path, focus order, labels, contrast, announcements.

responsive_behavior.description: Behavior at mobile/tablet/desktop breakpoints; what collapses, what hides.

content_i18n.description: User-facing copy requirements, tone, localization/i18n needs, date/number/currency formats.

architecture_notes.description: How this item fits the system: components touched, patterns to follow, references to architecture.decision_records.

api_contract.x-instructions: Full contract per endpoint; shapes as TypeScript-ish or JSON examples. Tenant scoping must be explicit in auth.

fields.description: name: type, nullability, default, constraints — one string per field.

db_changes.description: Schema deltas this item introduces (new table, column, index, backfill). Drives migration_steps.

events_and_jobs.description: Async work: emitted events, webhooks consumed, scheduled/background jobs, queues, retry semantics.

third_party_integrations.description: External services used, API versions, sandbox-vs-live handling, failure fallback.

feature_flag.description: Flag name gating this item, or 'none'. Flagged items must define both flag states' behavior.

config_and_secrets.description: Env vars and secrets required, per environment; mark which the human must provision.

permissions_model.description: Which roles can do what within this item; deny-by-default statement.

code_location_hints.description: Suggested paths/modules for the build session; advisory, not binding.

performance_targets.x-instructions: Concrete numbers: p95 latency, page-load budget, throughput, expected data volumes at 12 months. Inherit app-wide defaults if the BRD is silent, and say so.

availability_slo.description: Uptime target and degradation behavior if this item's dependencies are down.

security_requirements.x-instructions: Item-specific threats and controls: input validation, authz checks, tenant isolation proof, OWASP Top-10 relevance, encryption at rest/in transit.

privacy_compliance.description: PII touched, lawful basis if applicable, GDPR/CCPA duties (export, deletion), audit logging obligations.

observability.description: What gets logged/metered/traced for this item; alert thresholds; dashboards to update. Feeds hypercare monitoring.

rate_limits_and_quotas.description: Abuse and fairness controls: per-user/per-tenant limits, plan-tier quotas, 429 behavior.

cost_considerations.description: Anything with meaningful variable cost (LLM calls, email volume, storage, third-party per-seat fees) and its cap.

test_strategy.x-instructions: Which test layers apply and why; what is explicitly NOT tested and why. Financial/billing math always gets unit tests with hand-computed expected values.

unit_tests.description: Named cases for pure logic: rules, calculations, validators — including the edge_cases above.

integration_tests.description: API + DB + third-party (mocked/sandboxed) cases, including authz denial and cross-tenant isolation checks.

e2e_scenarios.description: Browser-level user journeys derived from acceptance_criteria; note which run in CI vs pre-release only.

test_data_requirements.description: Fixtures/seeds needed, multi-tenant test setup, anonymization rules if production-like data is used.

qa_signoff_criteria.description: Objective bar to flip status to qa_passed: all AC green, no open sev-1/2 defects, a11y checks pass, perf within targets.

deployment_notes.description: Anything nonstandard about shipping this item: ordering vs other items, flag ramp plan, cache invalidation, infra changes.

migration_steps.description: Ordered, idempotent steps for schema/data changes, with expand-migrate-contract pattern where the change is breaking.

rollback_plan.x-instructions: Required for every item. How to revert code AND data if this item fails in production; 'redeploy previous release' is acceptable only when there are no db_changes.

cutover_tasks.description: Item-specific go-live steps that roll up into cutover_plan.runbook (e.g. enable live payment keys, switch webhook URLs, user comms).

hypercare_watch.description: The specific signals to watch for THIS item after go-live and what 'healthy' looks like. Rolls up into hypercare_plan.monitoring.

success_metrics.description: Item-level measures of 'it worked' (adoption, conversion, error-free rate), linked to product_overview.success_metrics where possible.

runbook_notes.description: Operational knowledge for whoever supports this in production: common failure modes, how to diagnose, safe manual interventions.
